title: Cabin Floor Panel Support — Metallic Repair at the Mid Cabin Monument Positions
abstract: Metallic repair of corroded or deformed floor panel supports at the mid cabin monument positions, where spillage and repeated monument removal produce local damage under the lavatory and galley footprints.

sections.purpose: This repair covers corrosion and local deformation of the floor panel supports at the mid cabin monument positions, found when a lavatory or galley monument is removed for cabin work.
sections.damage_assessment: Lift the floor panels and clean the support flanges. Examine for corrosion under the monument footprint and for local deformation at the tie-down positions. The repair admits corrosion up to 0.4 millimetres deep after cleaning over a length not exceeding 200 millimetres per support, and deformation up to 1.5 millimetres out of flat. A support with corrosion through the flange, or with damage at more than two tie-down positions, is replaced rather than repaired. Check the drainage path below the monument at the same time; a support that has corroded once will corrode again if the drain is blocked, and the drain condition must be recorded with the repair.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend the corroded area inside the depth limit, keeping the blend faired and free of sharp edges. Where deformation is present, support the flange from below and dress it flat with the forming tool. Clean, apply the chemical conversion coating and the primer. Install the doubler strap over the blended length, positioned as shown on the repair drawing, and install the fasteners wet with faying surface sealant. Where a tie-down position is affected, install the cleat at that position with the current fastener standard. Seal the repair perimeter continuously so that spillage cannot enter the faying surface, and restore the floor covering and the monument seal on reassembly.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the repair whenever the monument is removed, and at least at every C check where the monument is not disturbed. Confirm the perimeter seal is continuous and the drain path is clear at every inspection. There is no life limit, but a repair that shows corrosion at its perimeter within 6 000 flight hours must be reported with the drainage condition.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Corrosion up to 0.4 mm deep after cleaning over not more than 200 mm per support; deformation up to 1.5 mm out of flat; not more than two tie-down positions affected.

repair_drawings.title: Floor panel support doubler strap and tie-down cleat, mid cabin monument positions

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single row at 25 mm pitch along the strap, 12 mm edge distance, staggered at the cleat positions
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit. Detailed visual inspection at every monument removal and at every C check, with the drainage condition recorded each time.
